title: Datasource spec
description: A connection spec. Secrets are referenced by ${ENV_VAR} placeholders and resolved from the environment at apply — never stored in the file.

type.description: Connector kind, e.g. snowflake | databricks | postgres | sql | csv | parquet | json | excel.

file.description: For a file-based type (csv/parquet/json/…): path to a LOCAL file, relative to this datasource file. At apply, `px` uploads it to the workspace disk and connects it. Omit for connection-style sources.

diskPath.description: Optional subdirectory under the workspace disk/ to upload `file` into (must exist server-side).

host.description: Connection-style sources: the database host (e.g. databases.prometheux.ai). For an object store (csv/parquet on S3), this MUST be the FULL directory that contains the files, e.g. 's3a://bucket/airports' — NOT just the bucket. If you split it (host='s3a://bucket', database='airports') the connect succeeds but the stored bind drops the subdirectory and the concept fails at RUN time with PATH_NOT_FOUND. For S3 do not set `database`.

port.description: Connection port, e.g. 5432 (postgres), 3306 (mariadb), 8123 (clickhouse), 1025 (teradata). Use 0 (or omit) for object-store/file sources.

password.description: Connection password — use a ${ENV_VAR} placeholder, resolved at apply, never a literal.

database.description: Database/catalog name (e.g. prometheux, pmtx_data). Omit for object-store (S3) sources — put the full path in `host` instead.

tables.description: The table(s) this datasource binds. Author ONE table per datasource file so the concept binds it unambiguously (a DB connect returns the whole group). Use the fully-qualified name for a database (e.g. 'prometheux.public.companies') or the file name for an object store (e.g. 'air-routes-nodes.csv').

s3aAccessKey.description: Object-store access key — use a ${ENV_VAR} placeholder.

s3aSecretKey.description: Object-store secret key — use a ${ENV_VAR} placeholder.

useHeaders.description: csv only: 'true' when the first row is a header.
